transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

A 'rattly growl' combined with weak suction on a 12-year-old Henry often points to either a partial blockage stressing the motor or worn motor bearings. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum. Detach the hose from the main body and look through it to check for blockages. Also, try to isolate whether the rattling sound is coming from the floorhead (brush bar area) or the main motor unit. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Thank you. I dropped a coin through the hose and it went straight through, so there is no blockage there. The suction is weak at both the hose end and at the head, so I don't think it is the floorhead making the noise.

[Heading: Likely internal blockage or worn motor bearings]
A 'rattly growl' with weak suction often means either something is partially blocking the internal cyclone/bin inlet (causing the motor to labour) or the motor bearings/fan are worn out. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum. Remove the bag and filters, then look into the bin inlet with a torch. Check for any debris stuck in the cyclone and ensure all rubber seals on the lid are seated correctly. For a quick test, try running it briefly with just the motor exposed (no bag/filter) to see if suction improves—if it does, you have an internal blockage or clogged filter housing. If the noise persists and suction remains weak even then, the motor bearings are likely worn.

Thank you. The bag and filter were both fitted correctly last week, and I'm a little nervous about running it without them. I should also mention that after about five minutes it gives off a hot, burning electrical smell, and in the dim hall I saw sparks flickering inside through the grille on top. Is it still safe to run it like that?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Stop using the vacuum immediately. Do not plug it in again. Seeing sparks inside the casing combined with a burning smell is a serious safety hazard. This indicates an active electrical fault, such as arcing wiring or failing motor windings, which poses a significant fire risk. Because this involves internal mains components and potential damage to the motor's insulation, it is not safe for you to attempt any further checks or repairs. Please unplug the machine from the wall socket (if you haven't already) and leave it disconnected. You will need to have it assessed by a qualified appliance engineer or consider replacement given its age.
